open_points.subject: EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS
open_points.text: “the conclusion each NodeExecution status gives (A13 rules 5 and 7)”
open_points.question: What single table value applies to `outcome_unknown`, whose conclusion instead varies with its EffectAttempt: waiting while `unknown`, succeeded when resolved `applied` without outputs, failed with `applied_outputs_unknown` when resolved `applied` with outputs, and ready for another attempt when resolved `not_applied`; and does the table or `effects.operation_element_conclusion` take precedence?
options: Map `outcome_unknown` to a special deferred/dynamic conclusion resolved by `effects`
Exclude operation statuses whose conclusions require EffectAttempt state, despite the stated totality
Map only the unresolved state and let `effects.operation_element_conclusion` override it after resolution
open_points.default_guess: Map `outcome_unknown` to a deferred conclusion and treat `effects.operation_element_conclusion` as authoritative for operation elements.

open_points.subject: EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS
open_points.text: “a table here keyed by the enumeration, total over its members, whose cells name members”
open_points.question: Which model enumeration supplies the cell values for `EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS`, and what are its complete members? No NodeExecution-conclusion enumeration is defined in the accepted models.
options: Add a node-conclusion enumeration containing success, failure, waits, skip, refusal and dynamic/deferred cases
Use NodeExecution status members themselves as the values
Use a structured result rather than one enumeration member
open_points.default_guess: Introduce a distinct node-conclusion enumeration covering succeeded, failed, skipped, waiting, refused and deferred operation outcomes.

open_points.subject: NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS
open_points.text: “what each node conclusion means for the run and for its dependants (A13 rules 5 and 7)”
open_points.question: What are the exact row keys, columns and cell values of `NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS`? The text does not define the node-conclusion taxonomy or how one row represents distinct consequences such as delivering outputs, blocking dependants, producing `upstream_failed`, propagating `skipped_by_guard`, ending the run `refused`, or contributing to final run success/failure.
options: One row per node conclusion with separate run-contribution and dependant-effect columns
Separate tables for run contribution and dependant propagation
One structured effect value per conclusion
open_points.default_guess: Use one row per explicit node conclusion with separate run-contribution and dependant-effect fields.

open_points.subject: HTTP_METHOD_BODIES
open_points.text: “whether an HTTP method carries a body … is a correspondence over that taxonomy … whose cells name members”
open_points.question: What model enumeration do the cells of `HTTP_METHOD_BODIES` name? The methods are model enumeration members, but body presence is described only as a yes/no property and no body-policy enumeration is defined.
options: A new body-policy enumeration such as `body` and `no_body`
HTTP-method members grouped into body-carrying and bodyless sets rather than a keyed table
open_points.default_guess: Use Boolean values keyed by every HTTP-method member, despite the statement that cells name enumeration members.
